methodology.description: Public draft-helper PPR redraft board. Player value and market cost are intentionally kept separate. Rankings blend broad expert consensus, current projections, recent independent expert boards and material preseason/news context; ADP is treated as price rather than player quality. League scoring, roster construction, draft slot, drafted players, positional scarcity and next-pick pressure are applied by the client recommendation engine.
rankingInputs: FantasyPros 2026 PPR expert consensus, ECR/ADP pages and late-August riser/faller coverage checked Aug. 28
ESPN Field Yates Top 160, Aug. 27 sleepers/busts/breakouts package and Aug. 28 NFL news
CBS Sports consensus/mocks and SportsLine sleeper/breakout/bust model updates through Aug. 28
RotoWire PPR rankings and late-August draft strategy coverage checked Aug. 28
Reuters, Rams/team reporting and independent beat coverage for Aug. 27-28 injury, trade and discipline developments
FantasyPros consensus projections and current aggregated PPR ADP
methodology.marketInput: Current FantasyPros aggregated PPR ADP remains the primary market-price input, cross-checked against CBS, ESPN and RotoWire. ADP is a price signal, not a substitute for player value. No broad Aug. 28 ADP move was large enough to override the player-value board by itself.
newsInputs: Puka Nacua receives a modest value discount because potential NFL discipline remains unresolved. The Rams' Aug. 27 trade to reacquire Tutu Atwell reignited speculation, although Sean McVay explicitly said the move was for receiver depth and had nothing to do with a possible Nacua suspension. ESPN had previously reported that a Week 1 suspension remained within the range of outcomes. The uncertainty is now explicitly priced rather than ignored.

Kenneth Walker III remains a top-20-range value but confidence is slightly lower after missing two practices with ankle swelling. Andy Reid described the issue as cleat-related and not expected to be serious, so this widens risk rather than triggering another major rank reversal.

Malik Nabers remains at No. 24 after briefly leaving practice Aug. 27. Giants coach John Harbaugh said there was no injury, and no credible follow-up report established a setback, so the recovery trend toward Week 1 remains intact.

Ashton Jeanty remains at No. 21. The ankle sprain still creates Week 1 uncertainty, but current reporting continues to describe him as on the mend and not facing a clearly established long-term absence.
Omarion Hampton's No. 19 rank remains supported by broad breakout backing, including four ESPN analysts naming him a 2026 breakout candidate on Aug. 27.
No other new suspension, trade, depth-chart demotion, preseason-usage shock or top-30 injury development found through the morning of Aug. 28 justified a larger public-board move.
methodology.notes: Expert disagreement is preserved with expertLow/expertHigh ranges; unresolved injuries, discipline risk and genuine model disagreement can intentionally widen those ranges. Confidence reflects agreement plus news certainty, not ceiling. The Aug. 28 refresh explicitly prices Puka Nacua's unresolved discipline risk and slightly widens Kenneth Walker III's injury range while keeping market/ADP separate from player value. This file is used only by smhillis/sleeper-draft-helper-public and must not be copied into or used to modify Scott's personal Sleeper Draft Assistant.

players.name: Puka Nacua
players.news: Moved from No. 3 to No. 4 to explicitly price unresolved NFL discipline risk. McVay says the Tutu Atwell trade was for depth and unrelated to a possible suspension, but prior ESPN reporting said a Week 1 ban remained possible. Elite underlying value remains intact; uncertainty widens the downside range.

players.name: James Cook III
players.news: Strong human-expert support remains in place and ESPN's Aug. 26 mock took him seventh overall, but SportsLine's current model is a meaningful bearish outlier and ranks him closer to a late-second/third-round RB value.

players.name: Christian McCaffrey
players.news: Returned to practice Aug. 23 after nearly three weeks sidelined by generalized tightness. Week 1 remains the target; injury risk is reduced, not erased.

players.name: Chris Olave
players.news: Jordyn Tyson's hamstring issue improves Olave's already strong target-volume outlook.

players.name: Rashee Rice
players.news: NFL closed its investigation with no additional discipline. Knee recovery remains the main risk, materially reducing the prior suspension discount.

players.name: Omarion Hampton
players.news: Broad breakout support strengthened again Aug. 27: four ESPN analysts named Hampton a 2026 breakout candidate. His current market price is broadly aligned with the public-board value rather than materially ahead of it.

players.name: Kenneth Walker III
players.news: Still supported as a top-20-range value, but missed two practices with ankle swelling and will sit the preseason finale. Andy Reid described the swelling as cleat-related and not expected to be serious, so the rank holds while confidence and the downside range worsen slightly.

players.name: Ashton Jeanty
players.news: Remains discounted after the ankle sprain. Current reporting still describes him as on the mend without a confirmed long-term absence, but Week 1 uncertainty remains enough to keep him below market.

players.name: Malik Nabers
players.news: Briefly exited Aug. 27 practice with a trainer, but coach John Harbaugh said there was no injury. No credible follow-up report established a setback, so Week 1 optimism remains while the wide expert range is preserved.
